option_relations.rationale: Acute on Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF) is a clinical syndrome, not directly equivalent to or a subtype/supertype of Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection. While HCV can cause ACLF, the option itself is not the infection.
Acute-on-chronic liver failure due to acute hepatitis C virus infection describes a complication where the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection is the underlying cause of the acute liver failure.
Hepatitis C virus infection is directly equivalent to the leaf 'Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection'.
Acute Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection is a specific subtype or stage of the broader 'Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection'.
